g1.E1_quote: κᵢ = 1 − βᵢ ... d²r/dt² = κᵢ [ −G M_S r/|r|³ + Σ ... ]
g1.E2_quote: Law 4c: "If a faint body passes within D = 0.1 L of Tellus or a P, then at the moment of closest approach ... its β is replaced by β_after = 0 ± 0.016"; "β changes only at close encounters (≲ 0.2 L)"
g1.E3_quote: "β is replaced by β_after = 0 ± 0.016" (a reset toward 0, stated as a rule, rather than a smooth evening-out)
g1.E4_quote: No conservation statement; "I have no law for the size of the change"; "mechanism behind κ ≠ 1 is unknown"
g1.notes: E3 granted because beta toward 0 counts per rubric; the change is an instantaneous reset, not exponential relaxation.

g2.E1_quote: d2r/dt2 = -(1 - beta_i) G m_S r/|r|^3 + sum ... (factor on S's pull only)
g2.E2_quote: Only orbit changes at encounters attributed to deflection: "long-term orbits change at planetary encounters"; beta treated as constant: "beta values that change from apparition to apparition ... (then beta is not a constant)"

g3.E1_quote: d²r_b/dt² = (1 + η_b) · Σ_{j≠b} G m_j (r_j − r_b) / |r_j − r_b|³
g3.E2_quote: "η is the same at every return of a body"; falsifier: "η changing from return to return"
g3.E4_quote: "a faint body's 'gravitational charge' is (1+η_b) times its inertia" is only a parenthetical interpretation, no exchange/conservation

g4.E1_quote: d²x/dt² = (1 − β) · Σ_j G m_j (r_j − x)/|r_j − x|³
g4.E2_quote: "dβ/dt = − A · β · Σ_p exp( −(d_p/R)² )"; "β changes only at close approaches to a planet"
g4.E3_quote: "β changes only at close approaches to a planet, always towards zero"
g4.E4_quote: "I have no physical explanation for β or for why planets erase it"; no conserved quantity or mass weighting
g4.notes: Closest to true law (Gaussian-window decay of beta toward 0), but beta of the planets is taken as 0 fixed, so not an f-difference law.

g5.E1_quote: "n^2 a^3 = K * GM_S, where K = GM_body/GM_S"; "K_N = 1.326" (per-body constant, framed as the body's own GM, not a multiplier of attraction felt)
g5.E2_quote: Only speculation: "perturbations by planets at close approaches"; no law
g5.notes: Analyst frames K as the body's GM ratio in a Kepler fit, not a force multiplier; partial at best.

g6.E1_quote: d^2 x/dt^2 = (1 - beta_k) * sum_{j in S,E,M,P1..P5} GM_j (r_j - x) / |r_j - x|^3
g6.E2_quote: Constant: "per-body constant k = 1 - beta"; falsifier "A faint body whose k changes in time"

g7.E2_quote: Only "kicks from Tellus's gravity at close approach" (orbital elements change), no factor
g7.notes: Kepler fits per window; no per-body pull factor.

g8.E1_quote: d²r_k/dt² = κ_k Σ_j GM_j (r_j − r_k)/|r_j − r_k|³
g8.E2_quote: "κ is constant in time for each body"; only a speculative hedge that "κ or the orbit changes slowly or in episodes"
